intelligence.human_view: The scorecard is the diagnosis, and the diagnosis is precise: the copy is authentic and full of personality (9 and 9) and the invitation is strong (9) — but trustworthiness is the lowest mark (6), and trustworthiness is the whole job of an entrance. A stranger meeting the agreement for the first time does not need to be told we are legit — "You're legit, we're legit, it's all legit" tells them nothing they can check, and "scam- and hacker-resistant to the max" is a claim with no proof behind it, and "if you're not legit, it won't be good" threatens the very person we are welcoming. The 10-star version does the opposite: it shows the reasons. "Welcome. Let's begin with trust." "Hi, I'm Naya." "Before you become part of our world, I want you to understand exactly what you're joining." "Because the foundation of a great community isn't technology. It's trust." Free to join. Privacy matters, choices matter, intelligence should serve you. Honesty, fairness, respect, doing no harm. Fraud, security, and abuse taken seriously — meaningful safeguards, improved continuously, accountable when something goes wrong. "No tricks. No hidden agenda. No promises of perfection." "We'd rather earn your trust than simply ask for it." Every line is a reason, not a declaration — and the last line is the rule itself: earn it, don't declare it. The 18:15Z refinement protects the work: the word count is already perfect, the flow keeps the page structured, the look stays — only the wording changes, plus Naya's portrait beside the welcome (harvested verbatim, never regenerated), because she is the one saying "Hi, I'm Naya" and the picture belongs next to those words. And the 18:17Z label decision is the same rule applied to the buttons: "Begin the deck" means nothing to a stranger; "Begin the visual story" is plain — that is not a question, it is the answer (SN-2992).
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you're welcoming a new friend to your house, and the first thing you say is "TRUST ME, my house is the best and safest house ever, and if you're not a good person it won't be good for you!" — that doesn't make them feel welcome at all, does it? It makes them nervous! The better way is to SHOW them: "Hi, I'm Naya! Come in, let me show you around — here's who we are, here's what we believe, here's what we promise. No tricks, no secrets. We'd rather EARN your trust than just ask for it." That's the new welcome — it gives people REASONS to trust us instead of just telling them to! And the buttons say what they really do now: "Begin the visual story" — because "Begin the deck" means nothing to someone who's never seen a deck before!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine you're welcoming someone into your home, dear, and the first words out of your mouth are "trust me, this is the safest house, and if you're not legit it won't be good for you!" — oh, love, that doesn't make anyone feel welcome, it makes them want to leave! The better way, dear, is to show them: "Welcome, let's begin with trust. Hi, I'm Naya — before you join our world, let me show you exactly what you're joining, who we are, what we stand for." Give them REASONS to trust you, love — free to join, honest, fair, respectful, doing no harm, no tricks, no hidden agenda — "we'd rather earn your trust than simply ask for it." That's the new welcome, dear: earn it, don't declare it. And the buttons say plainly what they do now, love — "Begin the visual story" — because "Begin the deck" means nothing at all to a stranger.
intelligence.naya_view: Agreement entrance scorecard — 7.5/10, not 10-star yet. The fix: stop telling people they can trust us — give them REASONS to trust us. No unverified "scam- and hacker-resistant to the max", no threatening "if you're not legit, it won't be good", no unexplained "law of one". His 10-star version is adopted: "Welcome. Let's begin with trust." "Hi, I'm Naya." "It's trust." Free to join. Honesty, fairness, respect, do no harm. "No tricks. No hidden agenda. No promises of perfection." "We'd rather earn your trust than simply ask for it." The look stays; only the wording changes, plus Naya's portrait beside the welcome. Buttons decided: "Begin the visual story" / "Read the Collective Agreement".
